2026-10-05.note: Moved from Sunday. Slow cooker on this afternoon; keep 4 portions in the fridge for Tuesday

ingredients: 1 veg stock cube, dissolved in 600ml hot water
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: For the best flavour, soften the onions, garlic, carrots and celery in the oil in a frying pan for 8 minutes. If you're short on time, put them straight into the slow cooker instead.
Put the veg, rinsed lentils, passata, tomato purée, herbs and stock into the slow cooker. Stir well and season.
Cook on high for 3–4 hours (or low for 6–7 hours), stirring once if you can, until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Take out Mathilda's portion and the 4 portions for Tuesday before adding any extra pepper or chilli to the rest.
About 15 minutes before tea, cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes and drain.
Serve the sauce over the spaghetti with grated cheese.
Cool Tuesday's 4 portions within an hour, then cover and keep in the fridge (no need to freeze for tomorrow).
recipe.tip: Red lentils soak up a lot of liquid in the slow cooker, which is why there's extra stock. Mathilda: mash her lentils a little finer if she's fussy about texture.

2026-10-06.meal: Reheat: Monday's lentil bolognese with spaghetti
2026-10-06.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 portions of Monday's lentil bolognese (from the fridge)
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Tip the bolognese into a pan with a splash of water and heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8–10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes while the sauce heats.
Serve with grated cheese. Anyone back late from hockey can have their portion microwaved separately.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving.

2026-10-07.meal: Air-fryer veggie sausages with crispy potato wedges & beans
2026-10-07.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — air fryer gets tea done fast either side of the run

ingredients: 1/2 tsp smoked paprika (for the grown-ups' wedges)
steps: Toss the potato wedges in the oil, season, and air fry at 200°C for 12 minutes.
Add the paprika to the wedges for the grown-ups now, keeping Mathilda and Francis's plain.
Add the veggie sausages to the air fryer basket alongside the wedges and cook for a further 8-10 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and the wedges are crisp.
Heat the beans in a small pan or the microwave for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the sausages and wedges with the beans.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her sausage into coins and keep her wedges plain. Ready in 20 minutes either side of hockey academy.

2026-10-08.meal: Fish finger pitta pockets with slaw
2026-10-08.note: Moved from Monday. Early, quick tea before Francis's parents' evening appointment at 7:05pm

ingredients: 1/4 white or red cabbage, finely shredded
Ketchup or tartare sauce, to serve
steps: Air fry the fish fingers at 180°C for 10 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot. (Or oven at 200°C / 180°C fan for 12–15 minutes.)
While they cook, mix the cabbage and carrot with the mayonnaise and lemon juice to make the slaw. Season.
Warm the pittas briefly and split them open.
Fill each pitta with lettuce, 3 fish fingers and a spoonful of slaw.
Serve with ketchup or tartare sauce on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: fish fingers and pitta plain, slaw on the side so she can dip or avoid it. Cut her pitta into fingers.
